subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation BMI stand for?
questions.explain: BMI stands for Body Mass Index and is used to assess whether a person is a healthy weight for their height.

questions.q: How is Body Mass Index (BMI) calculated?
options: Weight in kg divided by height in metres squared
Height in metres divided by weight in kg
Weight in kg multiplied by height in metres
Weight in kg divided by height in metres
questions.explain: BMI is found by dividing a person's weight in kilograms by their height in metres squared (kg/m2).

questions.q: A person is classified as obese when their BMI is at or above which value?
questions.explain: A BMI of 30 or above is classified as obese, while 25 to 29.9 is classed as overweight.

questions.q: Coronary heart disease is mainly caused by the build-up of fatty deposits in which blood vessels?
questions.explain: Coronary heart disease occurs when fatty deposits (atheroma) narrow the coronary arteries that supply the heart with blood.

questions.q: Type 2 diabetes is caused by a problem controlling blood glucose linked to which hormone?
questions.explain: In type 2 diabetes the body does not produce enough insulin or the cells do not respond to it, so blood glucose is not controlled properly.

questions.q: Which type of diabetes is most closely linked to diet, obesity and lifestyle?
options: Both are equally linked to diet
questions.explain: Type 2 diabetes is strongly associated with being overweight, poor diet and inactivity, whereas type 1 is not caused by lifestyle.

questions.q: Which government resource shows the proportions of the different food groups needed for a balanced diet?
questions.explain: The Eatwell Guide is the current UK model showing how much of each food group should make up a healthy, balanced diet.

questions.q: How many portions of fruit and vegetables does the '5 A Day' campaign recommend each day?
questions.explain: The 5 A Day message encourages eating at least five 80g portions of a variety of fruit and vegetables each day.

questions.q: What is the maximum recommended salt intake for an adult per day?
questions.explain: Adults are advised to eat no more than 6g of salt per day to help protect health.

questions.q: A diet high in salt is most closely linked to increasing the risk of which condition?
questions.explain: Too much salt raises blood pressure, which increases the risk of coronary heart disease and stroke.

questions.q: Free sugars should make up no more than what percentage of a person's daily energy intake?
questions.explain: Current guidance recommends that free sugars provide no more than 5% of total daily energy intake.

questions.q: Eating too much of which type of fat is most strongly linked to raised blood cholesterol and heart disease?
questions.explain: A high intake of saturated fat raises blood cholesterol, increasing the risk of coronary heart disease.

questions.q: Which type of cholesterol is often described as the 'bad' cholesterol because it can lead to fatty deposits in the arteries?
questions.explain: LDL cholesterol is called 'bad' cholesterol because it deposits fat in the artery walls, raising the risk of heart disease.

questions.q: What is the recommended daily fibre intake for adults?
questions.explain: Adults are advised to eat around 30g of fibre a day to support digestion and reduce the risk of diet-related disease.

questions.q: Frequent consumption of sugary foods and drinks is a major cause of which condition?
questions.explain: Sugars are broken down by mouth bacteria to produce acid that attacks tooth enamel, causing dental caries.

questions.q: A person weighs 72 kg and is 1.5 m tall. What is their BMI?
questions.explain: BMI = 72 divided by 1.5 squared (2.25), which equals 32, placing them in the obese category.

questions.q: A client is overweight, very inactive and eats a diet high in saturated fat and salt. Which diet-related condition are they at greatest risk of developing?
questions.explain: Excess weight, inactivity and a diet high in saturated fat and salt are key risk factors for coronary heart disease.

questions.q: Osteoporosis (weak, brittle bones) is most closely linked to a long-term lack of which nutrient?
questions.explain: A lack of calcium (along with vitamin D) over time reduces bone density and increases the risk of osteoporosis.

questions.q: To help someone increase their fibre intake, which food swap would you recommend?
options: Swap white bread for wholemeal bread
Swap wholemeal pasta for white pasta
Swap an apple for a sugary sweet
Swap water for a fizzy drink
questions.explain: Choosing wholemeal in place of white bread increases fibre intake and supports healthy digestion.

questions.q: A snack label shows it contains 40g of free sugars, but an adult's maximum is about 30g per day. What advice best promotes healthy eating?
options: It exceeds the daily maximum, so choose a lower-sugar alternative
It is fine because sugar gives quick energy
Eat two of them to reach the daily target
Sugar limits only apply to children
questions.explain: One snack providing 40g already exceeds the roughly 30g adult maximum for free sugars, so a lower-sugar choice is healthier.
